meta.description: 48 first-person clips of household tasks with per-frame 3D hand pose and natural-language action labels. ~1 GB. LeRobotDataset v3.0.

sample.pageIntro: Sample sets to verify the format and quality of data captured with the RootLens iOS app. New versions will be added as recording conditions and contributor scale expand.
sample.heroSubtitle: 48 first-person video clips of household tasks with per-frame 3D hand pose, wrist 6-DoF actions, and natural-language action labels.
sample.s1p1Lead: 48 clips of household tasks recorded with the RootLens iOS app from a head-mounted camera in Japan. All faces are blurred. Each frame contains:
s1p1Items: 21 hand joints in 3D per hand, in MANO canonical hand-local coordinates (`observation.hand_keypoints_3d`)
`task_index` into `meta/tasks.jsonl` pointing to a natural-language action label
sample.s2p1: LeRobotDataset v3.0 format. Standard loaders read this layout without modification.
sample.s3p1: Each frame's `task_index` maps to an action label in `meta/tasks.jsonl`. Labels are present-tense English sentences describing hand movements and objects (e.g. "Right hand reaches for the kettle handle."). Each clip is segmented into multiple labels at action transitions.
sample.s3p2: Labels are generated from video frames by a vision-language model.
sample.episodesSubheading: All 48 episodes. Click to play; expand a panel to read every action label with its timestamp.
sample.s4p1Lead: The next sample will add captures from roughly a dozen Japan-based TestFlight beta contributors:
s4p1Items: `observation.state` : camera 6-DoF in the ARKit world frame
`depth/{frame_index:06d}.png` : LiDAR depth maps on supported devices

hero.tagline: Film your day. Train robots. Get paid.
hero.description: A camera app where anyone can film household tasks and get paid when robot companies license the footage.

problem.title: Robots learn by watching people. But the footage barely exists.
problem.p1: Robot intelligence is evolving at an incredible pace. AI is going beyond language and images into physical action. Robots are learning to move by watching videos of people performing tasks.
problem.p2: But high-quality footage of real household tasks is extremely scarce. Collecting robot training data the traditional way requires expensive hardware, physical environments, and human operators.
problem.p3: Human action video is the critical bottleneck. That is why we are building RootLens.

appFlow.title: How it works

step1.label: Record
step1.text: Open the app and record yourself doing a household task. RootLens guides you to keep hands and objects in frame.

step2.label: Get verified
step2.text: Object detection scores the video automatically. Faces and personal text are blurred. The video is signed to prove it is real.

step3.label: Get paid
step3.text: Your verified recording enters the marketplace. Every time a robot company licenses your clip, you earn. Not once. Every time.

appFlow.editing: Every submission is focused, verified, and ready to use — not random video scraped from the web.

issues.title: Why RootLens data is valuable
issues.intro1: Robot companies can't train on random video. They need task-focused, hand-visible footage captured in real environments. And they need a lot of it, from as many different homes as possible.
issues.intro2: RootLens collects data from real kitchens, real laundry rooms, and real living spaces. Every home is different. Different layouts, different tools, different habits. This diversity is what helps robots generalize beyond the lab.
issues.pillarsLead: Each clip in our dataset is built on four pillars.

hands.label: Hand-focused capture
hands.text: Every video is framed around hands, objects, and actions. How you grip, how you move, how you use a tool. This is the data robots need to learn manipulation.

guidance.label: Real-time filming guidance
guidance.text: Collecting quality data for AI training is harder than it looks. The phone vibrates when hands drift out of frame. AI checks the scene before recording starts. You don't need to be a trained data collector. The app handles it.

scoring.label: Auto quality scoring
scoring.text: Every clip gets an objective quality score. Buyers can filter by score. Creators see exactly what makes a good clip and what doesn't. Better clips get licensed more, so quality improves on its own.

privacy.label: Privacy by default
privacy.text: When data comes from real homes filmed by real people, privacy isn't optional. Faces and text are automatically masked before anything leaves the device. Creators review and approve the blurred version before upload. Buyers receive clean, compliance-ready data.
